In the past I tried all Mint Desktops. From my experience I found KDE very nice and solid for gaming. The option to set different wallpapers for each desktop is a nicely added bonus as well. It has a built in launcher that you can create a dock on right on your desktop. No need to install Cairo-Dock. Gaming is solid and fast in KDE.

From using Cinnamon I found I ran into quite a few issues with compatibility. I don't recommend Cinnamon for gaming. Some games will not work no matter how hard you try. I couldn't even get some dependencies to install so this particular issue was baffling. It's still a great desktop for Developers and it seems like the Mint developers mainly use Cinnamon as it's always kept up to date over other distros.

I tried out XFCE and found it was extremely lightweight and fast. If you have a really old machine this might work out great for you. This is like a very minimalist OS so if you need other software apps you can always grab it from the Software center. Games did run very solid and fluid in this distro also.

My personal favorite is MATE. It's just all around the whole package for me. You can use Marco for minimal resources or turn on Compiz and make everything beautiful. All my games Wine, GoG, and native linux runs flawless on this distro. The reason I like MATE so much is even though I don't do exclusively gaming, it works well on other things I need as a desktop operating system. Everything I need is already installed and ready to go except for a dock. I installed Cairo-Dock on my desktop and it's golden. Compiz is a bit buggy but other than that it's a very solid daily use desktop.

Now all this is just based on my personal experience and I hope I can provide you some insight on what your next interface may be.
